resources.string: Reads e-passports (chip) and machine-readable passports (MRZ only). Everything stays on this phone.
NFC is on: e-passport chips can be read.
NFC is turned off. Turn it on to read e-passport chips.
This phone has no NFC. Only the MRZ (printed lines) can be read.

1. Point the camera at the passport photo page. The two lines of <<< text at the bottom (the MRZ) are read automatically.

2. e-passport (chip logo on the cover): hold the phone against the passport to read the chip, photo and security checks.

3. Passport without a chip (MRP): tap “No chip” to see the MRZ data.
Camera permission is needed to scan the passport.
Place the passport photo page inside the frame
Still looking. Try more light, avoid glare, move a little closer, or tap the screen to focus.
Hold the passport to your phone

Close the passport and lay the phone flat on the cover (or on the photo page for some countries). Move slowly until it vibrates, then keep still for 5 to 15 seconds.\n\nTip: remove thick or metal phone cases. The NFC antenna is usually in the middle of the phone’s back.
The chip rejected the key. The document number, date of birth or expiry date doesn’t match what’s printed. Check them and try again.
Connection lost. Keep the phone completely still on the passport and try again.
NFC is needed to read the chip.
Enter the document number and both dates as DD/MM/YYYY.
